q: The Wagon Repair Workshop at Bhusawal functions under which zonal railway?
e: The Wagon Repair Workshop at Bhusawal in Maharashtra functions under Central Railway, the zone in which Bhusawal division lies.

q: The Mechanical Workshop at Amritsar, one of the oldest workshops of Indian Railways, functions under which zonal railway?
e: The Mechanical Workshop at Amritsar in Punjab functions under Northern Railway, one of the oldest workshops in that zone.

q: The EMU Car Shed at Kurla in Mumbai, which maintains suburban electric multiple unit rakes, belongs to the:
e: The EMU Car Shed at Kurla in Mumbai maintains suburban EMU rakes of the Mumbai suburban system of Central Railway.

q: The Firozpur division, one of the largest divisions of Indian Railways, functions under which zonal railway?
e: The Firozpur division, among the largest divisions of Indian Railways, functions under Northern Railway and covers Punjab and adjoining areas.

q: In Indian Railways, the trackside system 'OMRS', used for detecting defects in rolling stock, stands for:
e: In Indian Railways, OMRS stands for Online Monitoring of Rolling Stock, the trackside system that detects defects in passing rolling stock.

q: In the medical department of Indian Railways, the computerised system 'HMIS', implemented in railway hospitals, stands for:
e: In the railway medical department, HMIS stands for Hospital Management Information System, the computerised system implemented in railway hospitals.

q: In Indian Railways, the web-based application 'IRPSM', used for processing and monitoring sanctioned works, stands for:

options.A: Indian Railways Projects Sanctions and Management
options.B: Indian Railways Planning and Scheduling Module
options.C: Integrated Railway Projects and Stores Management

e: In Indian Railways, IRPSM stands for Indian Railways Projects Sanctions and Management, the web-based application for processing and monitoring sanctioned works.

q: In railway reservation charts, the status 'RAC', allotted to waitlisted passengers, stands for:
e: In railway reservation charts, RAC stands for Reservation Against Cancellation, allotted to waitlisted passengers who may get a berth on cancellations.

q: In the computerised passenger reservation system, the ten-digit record number 'PNR' stands for:
e: In the passenger reservation system, PNR stands for Passenger Name Record, the ten-digit record number for a booking.

q: In railway signalling and train operations, the system 'CTC', which enables centralised control of signals and points over a section, stands for:
e: In railway signalling and train operations, CTC stands for Centralised Traffic Control, enabling centralised control of signals and points over a section.

q: In railway accident relief arrangements, the abbreviation 'ART', denoting the relief train rushed to an accident site, stands for:
e: In railway accident relief arrangements, ART stands for Accident Relief Train, the relief train rushed to an accident site with rescue equipment.

q: In the divisional administration of Indian Railways, 'ADRM' stands for:
e: In divisional administration of Indian Railways, ADRM stands for Additional Divisional Railway Manager, who assists the Divisional Railway Manager.

q: At a zonal railway headquarters, the rank of the head of a department denoted by 'PHOD' stands for:
e: At a zonal railway headquarters, PHOD stands for Principal Head of Department, the rank of the head of a department at that level.

q: In railway coaching stock, the coach code 'SLR' stands for:
e: In railway coaching stock, SLR stands for Seating cum Luggage Rake, a coach combining seating accommodation with a luggage compartment.

q: In railway engineering and level-crossing elimination works, the structure denoted by 'ROB' stands for:
e: In railway engineering and level-crossing elimination works, ROB stands for Road Over Bridge, a bridge carrying the road over the railway line.

q: In August 2023, the Prime Minister laid the foundation stone for the redevelopment of railway stations under the Amrit Bharat Station Scheme across the country, covering a total of:
e: In August 2023, the Prime Minister laid the foundation stone for redevelopment of 508 railway stations across the country under the Amrit Bharat Station Scheme.

q: In August 2025, the Prime Minister inaugurated the Sealdah-Esplanade section of the Kolkata Metro, thereby completing which corridor of the metro network?
e: In August 2025, the Prime Minister inaugurated the Sealdah-Esplanade section of the Kolkata Metro, thereby completing the East-West Metro corridor.

q: The Meerut Metro services, inaugurated in October 2025 along with the full Delhi-Meerut Namo Bharat corridor, are unique in the country because the metro trains run on:

options.A: The tracks of the Delhi Metro
options.C: The broad gauge lines of Northern Railway
options.D: The same infrastructure as the Namo Bharat RRTS trains

e: The Meerut Metro services inaugurated in October 2025 are unique because the metro trains run on the same infrastructure as the Namo Bharat RRTS trains on the Delhi-Meerut corridor.

q: India's first aluminium freight rake, inducted into service in October 2022, was flagged off from which railway station?
e: India's first aluminium freight rake, inducted in October 2022, was flagged off from Bhubaneswar railway station in Odisha.

q: India's first 'pod hotel' for railway passengers, offering capsule accommodation at the station, was opened in November 2021 at:
e: India's first pod hotel for railway passengers, offering capsule accommodation at the station, was opened in November 2021 at Mumbai Central.

q: The first 'Vande Metro' service, later renamed as the Namo Bharat Rapid Rail, flagged off in September 2024, was run between Ahmedabad and:
e: The first Vande Metro service, later renamed Namo Bharat Rapid Rail and flagged off in September 2024, was run between Ahmedabad and Bhuj.

q: The first air-conditioned EMU train service of the Chennai suburban network, introduced in April 2025, was run on the section between Chennai Beach and:
e: The first air-conditioned EMU service of the Chennai suburban network, introduced in April 2025, was run between Chennai Beach and Chengalpattu.

q: Commercial passenger operations on the first corridor of the Indore Metro commenced in the year:
e: Commercial passenger operations on the first corridor of the Indore Metro commenced in 2025, when the initial priority corridor section was opened.

q: The trains running on the Delhi-Ghaziabad-Meerut RRTS corridor were formally given the name 'Namo Bharat' in the year:
e: The trains on the Delhi-Ghaziabad-Meerut RRTS corridor were formally given the name Namo Bharat in 2023, replacing the earlier RAPIDX branding.

q: The first Vande Bharat Express service of Kerala, flagged off in April 2023, was run between Thiruvananthapuram Central and:
e: The first Vande Bharat Express service of Kerala, flagged off in April 2023, was run between Thiruvananthapuram Central and Kasaragod.

q: The Sanskrit epic poem 'Raghuvamsha', which traces the lineage of King Raghu and his descendants including Rama, was composed by:
e: Raghuvamsha, the Sanskrit epic poem tracing the lineage of King Raghu and his descendants including Rama, was composed by Kalidasa.

q: The Sanskrit play 'Uttararamacharita', which depicts the later life of Rama after his return to Ayodhya, was written by:
e: Uttararamacharita, the Sanskrit play depicting the later life of Rama after his return to Ayodhya, was written by Bhavabhuti.

q: The Sanskrit play 'Ratnavali', centred on Princess Ratnavali and King Udayana of Vatsa, is attributed to:
e: Ratnavali, the Sanskrit play centred on Princess Ratnavali and King Udayana of Vatsa, is attributed to King Harshavardhana.

q: The 'Sushruta Samhita', a foundational Sanskrit text of surgery and medicine, is traditionally attributed to:
e: The Sushruta Samhita, a foundational Sanskrit text of surgery and medicine, is traditionally attributed to Sushruta.

q: The 'Brihat Samhita', an encyclopaedic Sanskrit work covering astronomy, astrology, geography and many other subjects, was written by:
e: The Brihat Samhita, an encyclopaedic Sanskrit work on astronomy, astrology, geography and other subjects, was written by Varahamihira.

q: The 'Thirukkural', the celebrated Tamil work of couplets on ethics, polity and love, was composed by:
e: Thirukkural, the celebrated Tamil work of couplets on ethics, polity and love, was composed by Thiruvalluvar.

q: The Tamil epic 'Silappadikaram' (The Tale of an Anklet), centred on Kannagi and Kovalan, was composed by:
e: Silappadikaram, the Tamil epic centred on Kannagi and Kovalan, was composed by Ilango Adigal.

q: The Bengali novel 'Kapalkundala' (1866), the story of a girl brought up by a Kapalik in a forest by the sea, was written by:
e: Kapalkundala of 1866, about a girl brought up by a Kapalik in a forest by the sea, was written by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay.

q: The Bengali novella 'Parineeta' (1914), centred on the orphan girl Lalita and her guardian's family, was written by:
e: Parineeta of 1914, centred on the orphan girl Lalita and her guardian's family, was written by Sarat Chandra Chattopadhyay.

q: The pioneering feminist work 'Sultana's Dream' (1905), which imagines a world ruled by women, was written by:
e: Sultana's Dream of 1905, the pioneering feminist work imagining a world ruled by women, was written by Rokeya Sakhawat Hossain.

q: The Malayalam novel 'Indulekha' (1889), regarded as the first major novel in Malayalam, was written by:
e: Indulekha of 1889, regarded as the first major novel in Malayalam, was written by O. Chandu Menon.

q: The celebrated Hindi work 'Volga Se Ganga', a collection of historical stories tracing the journey of a people from the Volga to the Ganga, was written by:
e: Volga Se Ganga, the collection of historical stories tracing a people's journey from the Volga to the Ganga, was written by Rahul Sankrityayan.

q: The Hindi verse play 'Andha Yug', set on the last day of the Mahabharata war and its aftermath, was written by:
e: Andha Yug, the Hindi verse play set on the last day of the Mahabharata war and its aftermath, was written by Dharamvir Bharati.

q: The novel 'To the Lighthouse' (1927), centred on the Ramsay family and their visits to the Isle of Skye, was written by:
e: To the Lighthouse of 1927, centred on the Ramsay family and their visits to the Isle of Skye, was written by Virginia Woolf.

q: The novel 'The Trial', in which the bank clerk Josef K. is arrested and prosecuted for an unnamed crime, was written by:
e: The Trial, in which bank clerk Josef K. is arrested and prosecuted for an unnamed crime, was written by Franz Kafka.

q: The satirical war novel 'Catch-22' (1961), centred on the American bombardier Yossarian, was written by:
e: Catch-22 of 1961, the satirical war novel centred on American bombardier Yossarian, was written by Joseph Heller.

q: The Wanchoo Committee (1971), appointed by the Government of India, is mainly associated with an inquiry into:
e: The Wanchoo Committee of 1971 is mainly associated with an inquiry into direct taxes and unaccounted money, and recommended measures against tax evasion.

q: The Thungon Committee (1988) is associated with recommendations on the strengthening of:
e: The Thungon Committee of 1988 is associated with recommendations on strengthening Panchayati Raj institutions, including constitutional status for them.

q: The National Knowledge Commission, set up in 2005 to advise on policies for education, research and innovation, was chaired by:
e: The National Knowledge Commission, set up in 2005 to advise on education, research and innovation policy, was chaired by Sam Pitroda.

q: The Swaran Singh Committee (1976) is best known for recommending the inclusion in the Constitution of:

options.B: A separate chapter on environmental protection

e: The Swaran Singh Committee of 1976 is best known for recommending inclusion of the Fundamental Duties of citizens in the Constitution, added by the 42nd Amendment.

q: The Tarkunde Committee, appointed on the initiative of Jayaprakash Narayan, is associated with recommendations on:
e: The Tarkunde Committee, appointed on the initiative of Jayaprakash Narayan, is associated with recommendations on electoral reforms.

q: The Bibek Debroy Committee (2015) is associated with recommendations on:

options.A: The disinvestment of railway public sector undertakings
options.B: The restructuring and modernisation of Indian Railways
options.C: The pricing of passenger fares on Indian Railways
options.D: The merger of the Railway Budget with the General Budget

e: The Bibek Debroy Committee of 2015 is associated with recommendations on restructuring and modernisation of Indian Railways, including a regulator and private entry.

q: The Shah Nawaz Committee was appointed by the Government of India to inquire into:

options.A: The circumstances of the Jallianwala Bagh massacre
options.C: The disappearance of Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose
options.D: The excesses committed during the Emergency

e: The Shah Nawaz Committee was appointed to inquire into the disappearance of Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose and the circumstances of his reported death.

q: The Wadhwa Commission (1999) was appointed to inquire into:

options.B: The demolition of the disputed structure at Ayodhya
options.C: The riots that followed the assassination of Indira Gandhi
options.D: The murder of the missionary Graham Staines and his two sons in Odisha

e: The Wadhwa Commission of 1999 was appointed to inquire into the murder of missionary Graham Staines and his two sons in Odisha.

q: The Justice U. C. Banerjee Committee (2004) was set up by the Ministry of Railways to inquire into:

options.A: The fire on the Sabarmati Express at Godhra in 2002
options.B: The collision of trains at Gaisal in 1999
options.C: The derailment of the Howrah Rajdhani Express in 2002
options.D: The stampede at New Delhi railway station

e: The Justice U. C. Banerjee Committee of 2004 was set up by the Ministry of Railways to inquire into the fire on the Sabarmati Express at Godhra in 2002.

q: The Naresh Chandra Committee (2002) was set up by the Government of India to recommend reforms relating to:

options.A: The working of the capital markets
options.C: The governance of public sector banks

e: The Naresh Chandra Committee of 2002 was set up to recommend reforms relating to corporate audit and governance, including auditor independence and board practices.

q: The Second Finance Commission of India was chaired by:
e: The Second Finance Commission of India was chaired by K. Santhanam, succeeding the First Commission chaired by K. C. Neogy.

q: The Eighth Finance Commission of India was chaired by:
e: The Eighth Finance Commission of India was chaired by Y. B. Chavan, the former Maharashtra Chief Minister and Union Minister.

q: The Strait of Hormuz connects the Persian Gulf with the:
e: The Strait of Hormuz connects the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman, and is a key route for oil shipments from the Gulf region.

q: The Bosporus Strait in Turkey connects the Black Sea with the:
e: The Bosporus Strait in Turkey connects the Black Sea with the Sea of Marmara, passing through Istanbul.

q: The Kiel Canal in Germany connects the North Sea with the:
e: The Kiel Canal in Germany connects the North Sea with the Baltic Sea, shortening the route between them by avoiding the Danish peninsula.

q: The Chitrakote Falls, often called the Niagara of India, are located in Chhattisgarh on the river:
e: The Chitrakote Falls, often called the Niagara of India, are located in Chhattisgarh on the Indravati River in Bastar district.

q: Lake Titicaca, the highest navigable lake in the world, lies on the border between:
e: Lake Titicaca, the highest navigable lake in the world, lies on the border between Peru and Bolivia in the Andes.

q: Aconcagua, the highest mountain outside Asia, is located in the country of:
e: Aconcagua, the highest mountain outside Asia, is located in Argentina in the Andes range near the Chilean border.

q: The highest peak of Europe is:
e: The highest peak of Europe is Mount Elbrus in the Caucasus in Russia, which is higher than Mont Blanc in the Alps.

q: Mount Fuji, the highest mountain of Japan, is located on the Japanese island of:
e: Mount Fuji, the highest mountain of Japan, is located on Honshu, the largest Japanese island.

q: The River Danube, which flows through Vienna, Budapest and Belgrade, empties into the:
e: The River Danube, flowing through Vienna, Budapest and Belgrade, empties into the Black Sea through its delta in Romania.

q: The Namib Desert, regarded as the oldest desert in the world, lies mainly in the country of:
e: The Namib Desert, regarded as the oldest desert in the world, lies mainly in Namibia along its Atlantic coast.

q: Which country is known as the 'Land of the Thunder Dragon'?
e: Bhutan is known as the Land of the Thunder Dragon, from Druk Yul in its local language, where Druk means thunder dragon.

q: The Prime Meridian (0 degree longitude), from which longitudes are reckoned, passes through:
e: The Prime Meridian of 0 degree longitude, from which longitudes are reckoned, passes through Greenwich in London.

q: The Parliament of Iceland, one of the oldest parliamentary assemblies in the world, is known as the:
e: The Parliament of Iceland, one of the oldest parliamentary assemblies in the world, is known as the Althing.

q: The 'Kyat' is the currency of:
e: The Kyat is the currency of Myanmar, issued by the Central Bank of Myanmar and used for all domestic transactions there.

q: The escape velocity from the surface of the Earth is about:
e: The escape velocity from the surface of the Earth is about 11.2 km per second, the speed needed to escape Earth's gravity without further propulsion.

q: The headquarters of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) is located at:
e: The headquarters of the International Atomic Energy Agency is located at Vienna in Austria, at the Vienna International Centre.

q: 'Plaster of Paris', widely used for setting fractured bones and for making casts and moulds, is chemically:
e: Plaster of Paris, used for setting fractured bones and for casts and moulds, is chemically calcium sulphate, in its hemihydrate form.

q: The Railway Recruitment Control Board (RRCB), which coordinates and monitors the working of all Railway Recruitment Boards, was set up in the Ministry of Railways in the year:
e: The Railway Recruitment Control Board, which coordinates and monitors all Railway Recruitment Boards, was set up in the Ministry of Railways in 1998.

q: The Indian Railways Institute of Signal Engineering and Telecommunications (IRISET) at Secunderabad was established in the year:
e: The Indian Railways Institute of Signal Engineering and Telecommunications at Secunderabad was established in 1957 for training in signalling and telecom.

q: The Research Designs and Standards Organisation (RDSO) at Lucknow primarily functions as the:

options.A: Operating authority for all special trains of Indian Railways
options.B: Recruiting agency for the engineering services of Indian Railways
options.C: Technical adviser and consultant to Indian Railways for design and standardisation of equipment
options.D: Manufacturing unit for signalling equipment of Indian Railways

e: RDSO at Lucknow primarily functions as the technical adviser and consultant to Indian Railways for design and standardisation of equipment.

q: RITES Limited, the consultancy organisation of the Ministry of Railways, is categorised as a:
e: RITES Limited, the consultancy organisation of the Ministry of Railways, is categorised as a Schedule A Central Public Sector Enterprise.

q: The Western Dedicated Freight Corridor, being implemented by DFCCIL from Dadri to Jawaharlal Nehru Port, has a total route length of about:
e: The Western Dedicated Freight Corridor implemented by DFCCIL from Dadri to Jawaharlal Nehru Port has a total route length of about 1,506 km.

q: The inland container terminals operated by the Container Corporation of India (CONCOR) across the country are popularly known as:
e: The inland container terminals operated by CONCOR across the country are popularly known as dry ports, as they provide customs and container handling away from seaports.

q: The headquarters of the NCRTC, which implements the Regional Rapid Transit System (RRTS) corridors in the National Capital Region, is located at:
e: The headquarters of the NCRTC, which implements the RRTS corridors in the National Capital Region, is located at New Delhi.

q: The Mumbai-Ahmedabad High Speed Rail corridor, being executed by NHSRCL, will have a total of how many stations?
e: The Mumbai-Ahmedabad High Speed Rail corridor executed by NHSRCL will have a total of 12 stations along its 508 km route.

q: The National Academy of Indian Railways (NAIR) at Vadodara primarily imparts training to:

options.A: Only the officers of the Accounts Department
options.B: Probationers and serving officers of the various railway services
options.C: Only the officers of the Railway Protection Force

e: NAIR at Vadodara primarily imparts training to probationers and serving officers of the various railway services, not only one department.

q: At present, the Railway Claims Tribunal functions through how many benches located across the country?
e: The Railway Claims Tribunal at present functions through 23 benches located across the country for deciding railway compensation claims.

q: The Angus Works of Braithwaite and Company Limited, which manufactures cranes, foundry products and machinery components, is located in which district of West Bengal?
e: The Angus Works of Braithwaite and Company Limited, manufacturing cranes and foundry products, is located in Hooghly district of West Bengal.

q: The first Railway Service Commission, set up in 1942 for the recruitment of subordinate staff, was established for which railway?
e: The first Railway Service Commission, set up in 1942 for recruitment of subordinate staff, was established for the North Western Railway.

q: The headquarters of the Uttar Pradesh Metro Rail Corporation (UPMRC), which executes the metro rail projects of Lucknow, Kanpur and Agra, is located at:
e: The headquarters of the Uttar Pradesh Metro Rail Corporation, executing metro projects of Lucknow, Kanpur and Agra, is located at Lucknow.

q: The Research Designs and Standards Organisation (RDSO) became the first institution in India to be recognised as a Standard Developing Organisation (SDO) under the 'One Nation One Standard' mission in the year:
e: RDSO became the first institution in India recognised as a Standard Developing Organisation under the One Nation One Standard mission in 2021.

q: The diesel locomotive factory at Marhowra in Bihar has been set up as a joint venture of Indian Railways with:
e: The diesel locomotive factory at Marhowra in Bihar has been set up as a joint venture of Indian Railways with Wabtec, formerly GE Transportation.

q: The Diesel Loco Shed at Gandhidham in Gujarat functions under which zonal railway?
e: The Diesel Loco Shed at Gandhidham in Gujarat functions under Western Railway, the zone covering the Kutch area.

q: The first diesel locomotive was rolled out by the Diesel Locomotive Works (now Banaras Locomotive Works) at Varanasi in the year:
e: The first diesel locomotive was rolled out by the Diesel Locomotive Works, now Banaras Locomotive Works, at Varanasi in 1964.

q: The Rail Wheel Factory at Yelahanka, Bengaluru, which manufactures wheels, axles and wheel sets for Indian Railways, was inaugurated in the year:
e: The Rail Wheel Factory at Yelahanka, Bengaluru, manufacturing wheels, axles and wheel sets, was inaugurated in 1984.

q: The Mechanical Workshop at Izzatnagar (Bareilly), which undertakes periodic overhaul of coaches, functions under which zonal railway?
e: The Mechanical Workshop at Izzatnagar in Bareilly, undertaking periodic overhaul of coaches, functions under North Eastern Railway.

q: The Diesel Loco Shed at Andal in West Bengal functions under which zonal railway?
e: The Diesel Loco Shed at Andal in West Bengal functions under Eastern Railway, the zone covering the Asansol-Andal area.

q: The Konkan Railway line, running from Roha to Thokur, passes through which of the following groups of States?
e: The Konkan Railway line from Roha to Thokur passes through Maharashtra, Goa and Karnataka along the west coast.

q: The Wagon Workshop at Guntupalli, near Vijayawada, which undertakes periodic overhaul of freight wagons, functions under which zonal railway?
e: The Wagon Workshop at Guntupalli near Vijayawada, undertaking periodic overhaul of freight wagons, functions under South Central Railway.

q: In connection with the electric locomotive factory at Madhepura in Bihar, 'MELPL' stands for:

options.C: Madhepura Engine and Locomotive Plant Limited

e: In connection with the electric locomotive factory at Madhepura in Bihar, MELPL stands for Madhepura Electric Locomotive Private Limited.

q: The Diesel Loco Shed at Alambagh in Lucknow functions under which zonal railway?
e: The Diesel Loco Shed at Alambagh in Lucknow functions under Northern Railway, the zone covering Lucknow division.

q: In Indian Railways, the designation 'PCE', borne by the head of the civil engineering department at a zonal headquarters, stands for:
e: In Indian Railways, PCE stands for Principal Chief Engineer, the head of the civil engineering department at a zonal headquarters.

q: In Indian Railways, the designation 'PCME', borne by the head of the mechanical engineering department at a zonal headquarters, stands for:
e: In Indian Railways, PCME stands for Principal Chief Mechanical Engineer, the head of the mechanical engineering department at a zonal headquarters.

q: In Indian Railways, the designation 'PCEE', borne by the head of the electrical engineering department at a zonal headquarters, stands for:
e: In Indian Railways, PCEE stands for Principal Chief Electrical Engineer, the head of the electrical engineering department at a zonal headquarters.

q: In Indian Railways, the designation 'PCSTE', borne by the head of the signalling and telecommunication department at a zonal headquarters, stands for:

options.A: Principal Chief Safety and Traffic Engineer
options.B: Principal Chief Stores and Transport Engineer
options.C: Principal Chief Signal and Telecommunication Engineer
options.D: Principal Chief Systems and Telecom Engineer

e: In Indian Railways, PCSTE stands for Principal Chief Signal and Telecommunication Engineer, the head of the signalling and telecom department at a zonal headquarters.

q: In Indian Railways, the designation 'PCMM', borne by the head of the materials management department at a zonal headquarters, stands for:
e: In Indian Railways, PCMM stands for Principal Chief Materials Manager, the head of the materials management department at a zonal headquarters.

q: In Indian Railways, the designation 'PCSC', borne by the head of the security department (RPF) at a zonal headquarters, stands for:
e: In Indian Railways, PCSC stands for Principal Chief Security Commissioner, the head of the security department, the RPF, at a zonal headquarters.
